hints: Focus on reversing addition polymerisation, where each single bond in the chain came from a C=C double bond in an alkene monomer.
Split the four-carbon backbone into two two-carbon units: the left pair is -CH2-C(CH3)2- and the right pair is -CH(CH3)-CH2-.
Put a double bond back between the two carbons of each unit and add H atoms to complete the alkenes, then check their names.
walkthrough:
**Recognise an addition copolymer**

Think of this as two different alkenes joined together. To find them, we work backwards from polymer to monomers.

Rule to reverse it:
$$-CH_2-CH_2- \leftarrow CH_2=CH_2$$

**Split the section into two monomer units**

The backbone has four carbons, so cut it in the middle to give two C2 fragments.

$$-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2- \rightarrow [-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-] + [-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-]$$

**Restore the double bonds**

Now put the C=C back in each fragment. This gives the two starting alkenes.

$$-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2- \leftarrow CH_2=C(CH_3)_2$$
$$-CH(CH_3)-CH_2- \leftarrow CH_2=CH(CH_3)$$
The first is methylpropene (2-methylpropene) and the second is propene. That matches the copolymer section perfectly.

options.A: But-1-ene is $CH_2=CHCH_2CH_3$ and would give a repeat unit of $-CH_2-CH(CH_2CH_3)-$. There is no $-CH(CH_2CH_3)-$ ethyl branch in the given section, only methyl branches, so this cannot be correct.
options.B: But-2-ene is $CH_3CH=CHCH_3$ and would give $-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-$. The section has $-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-$ on the right, not two adjacent $CH(CH_3)$ groups, so but-2-ene does not fit.
options.C: Ethene $CH_2=CH_2$ would give $-CH_2-CH_2-$, with no branches. Pent-2-ene $CH_3CH=CHCH_2CH_3$ would give $-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_2CH_3)-$. Neither matches the branched $C(CH_3)_2$ carbon seen on the left of the section.
options.D: Methylpropene $CH_2=C(CH_3)_2$ polymerises to $-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-$ and propene $CH_2=CH(CH_3)$ polymerises to $-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-$, shown here as $-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-$. Joined together they give exactly $-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-$.
